case: Conflict-of-interest proceeding over his role in drafting 'Lex Agrokor'
type: administrative proceeding before the Commission for the Resolution of Conflicts of Interest (Plenković as the official concerned)
description: In September 2018 the Commission for the Resolution of Conflicts of Interest (Povjerenstvo za odlučivanje o sukobu interesa) opened proceedings against Plenković and Most leader Božo Petrov over their activities during the drafting of the 2017 law on extraordinary administration ('Lex Agrokor'); according to Dnevnik Nova TV, the case against Plenković concerned non-transparent communication with the public. The Commission was due to decide on 31 May 2019, but the day before Plenković requested the recusal of its president Nataša Novaković, arguing that she had worked at the Croatian Employers' Association (HUP), which is linked to Agrokor; Commission member Davorin Ivanjek called the late request an abuse of procedural rights (Index.hr). After the Administrative Court and the High Administrative Court declared themselves not competent, the Constitutional Court ruled that the Commission itself was competent to decide on the recusal. In 2021, after the High Administrative Court ruled with final effect in the case of the late Zagreb mayor Milan Bandić that the Commission could not decide on breaches of the general principles of office in Article 5 of the Conflict of Interest Act, the Commission suspended its proceedings against Plenković, Martina Dalić, Zdravko Marić and Božo Petrov; Novaković said they could be reopened if case law changed (Dnevnik Nova TV).
outcome: Proceedings suspended by the Commission in 2021 without a decision on the merits; no reopening reported as of October 2026.
court: Povjerenstvo za odlučivanje o sukobu interesa (Commission for the Resolution of Conflicts of Interest); Constitutional Court of Croatia (on the recusal question)
presumption_note: This was an administrative ethics proceeding, not a criminal case. No finding was made against Plenković: the proceedings were suspended before any decision on the merits.
key_facts: September 2018: proceedings opened against Plenković and Božo Petrov
30 May 2019: Plenković requests the recusal of the Commission's president
Constitutional Court: the Commission is competent to decide on the recusal
2021: proceedings suspended after the High Administrative Court's Bandić ruling on Article 5

case: Conflict-of-interest case over the appointment of his best man Igor Pokaz as ambassador to the United Kingdom (P-382/17)
type: administrative proceeding before the Commission (Plenković as the official concerned), then administrative lawsuit (Plenković as plaintiff)
description: The Commission opened proceedings against Plenković because, when career diplomat Igor Pokaz was appointed ambassador to the United Kingdom, he had not informed the bodies involved or the public that he had been best man (kum) at Pokaz's wedding. Plenković said that by the Commission's logic he would have to be excluded from all appointments in the diplomatic service, since those concerned were 'more or less his friends, acquaintances or colleagues' (N1). In 2019 the Commission decided by a majority that he had violated the principle of conscientious and transparent conduct, a finding that carries no penalty; member Aleksandra Jozić-Ileković dissented. Plenković sued the Commission before the Administrative Court in Zagreb, saying every citizen had the right to challenge decisions of public bodies he disagreed with (Dnevnik Nova TV). In 2020 the court (judge Vlaho Bassegli Gozze) ruled in his favour at first instance, holding that the Commission cannot rule on the principles of office in Article 5 unless they are linked to a specific statutory provision; the Commission announced an appeal to the High Administrative Court (Telegram). The judgment is published on the Commission's website.
outcome: Commission finding (2019) annulled at first instance by the Administrative Court in Zagreb (2020); the Commission announced an appeal. The final outcome of the appeal was not found in the sources available for this research.
court: Povjerenstvo za odlučivanje o sukobu interesa; Upravni sud u Zagrebu (Administrative Court in Zagreb); appeal announced to the Visoki upravni sud (High Administrative Court)
presumption_note: Administrative case, not a criminal one. The Commission's 2019 finding concerned principles of conduct, carried no sanction and was annulled at first instance; Plenković rejected any conflict of interest.
key_facts: Pokaz, a career diplomat, was appointed ambassador to the United Kingdom
2019: Commission finds by majority a breach of the principle of conscientious and transparent conduct
Plenković sues; 2020: Administrative Court in Zagreb rules in his favour at first instance

case: Conflict-of-interest case over documents on the government delegation's trip to the EPP meeting in Helsinki
type: administrative proceeding before the Commission (Plenković as the official concerned), then administrative lawsuit (Plenković as plaintiff)
description: Media asked who had paid for the trip of Plenković and several ministers aboard the government plane to a European People's Party meeting in Helsinki on 7–8 November 2018, and whether it was a government or an HDZ delegation. In 2019 the Commission launched proceedings against Plenković, Interior Minister Davor Božinović and former ministers Tomislav Tolušić, Nada Murganić and Lovro Kuščević because the travel documents it had requested were not submitted; Plenković said the government had sent everything requested ('I won't submit anything else') and that he had travelled as prime minister to meet Finland's prime minister (N1). In late 2019 the Commission decided not to open proceedings over the trip itself because it lacked the documents, but found by majority that the five had violated the principles of conduct by acting irresponsibly and non-transparently over the documents (N1). Plenković challenged that decision before the Administrative Court in Zagreb, which ruled in his favour in March 2020 on the same reasoning as in the Pokaz case; the Commission said it would appeal (Telegram).
outcome: Commission finding annulled at first instance by the Administrative Court in Zagreb (March 2020); the Commission announced an appeal. The final outcome was not found in the sources available for this research.
court: Povjerenstvo za odlučivanje o sukobu interesa; Upravni sud u Zagrebu (Administrative Court in Zagreb)
presumption_note: Administrative case, not a criminal one. The Commission made no finding on the trip itself; its finding on the handling of documents carried no sanction and was annulled at first instance.
key_facts: 7–8 November 2018: trip to the EPP meeting in Helsinki on the government plane
2019: proceedings launched over undelivered travel documents
Late 2019: no case on the trip itself; majority finding of breach of principles over the documents
March 2020: Administrative Court in Zagreb rules for Plenković; appeal announced

case: Commission proceeding over inconsistencies in his asset declarations for 2016–2018
type: administrative proceeding before the Commission (Plenković as the official concerned)
description: In early October 2021 the Commission opened proceedings against Plenković because his asset declarations for 2016 to 2018 had overstated the salary income declared for his spouse compared with the amounts actually received. On 17 June 2022 the Commission unanimously imposed a fine of HRK 3,000, payable in three equal instalments, for the inconsistencies in his asset declaration, as confirmed by its president Nataša Novaković (tportal, citing Dnevnik.hr).
outcome: Fine of HRK 3,000 imposed by the Commission on 17 June 2022 (payable in three instalments).
court: Povjerenstvo za odlučivanje o sukobu interesa (Commission for the Resolution of Conflicts of Interest)
presumption_note: This was an administrative proceeding on the accuracy of asset declarations, not a criminal case; the sanction was an administrative fine. No court challenge was mentioned in the reports consulted.
key_facts: 17 June 2022: unanimous decision, fine of HRK 3,000 in three instalments
